title: How many edges can be removed from a flower snark line graph?
scope: For every odd q >= 5: the largest removable edge set of L(J_q) has 9 edges and the 9-edge removable sets are exactly the 4q claw sets; q = 3: maximum 15. Counts of removable k-sets for q >= 7. No claim about other snarks.
gate_basis: snark_check.py (Python standard library) recomputes the transfer matrices, checks T^2 = T^4 and the twist symmetry for all 4096 unit subsets, the far-pairs lemma, the exhaustive window search, the cases q = 3, 5, and claw validity for q <= 41; it compares the transfer model with direct colouring of L(J_q) - R for all |R| <= 2 and q = 3, 5, 7. extras.py gives the counts and the Petersen case. Logs in evidence/logs/. One independent AI referee pass.
dependencies: Python 3.8+ standard library for snark_check.py and extras.py.
OR-Tools (CP-SAT) and a C compiler for the exploratory programs in evidence/search/.
limitations: Not externally peer reviewed. Checks so far: the stand-alone program, independent brute-force computations, and one independent AI referee pass on 2026-11-17. One independent AI referee (another agent) rebuilt the graphs, a SAT colourability test and the transfer matrices from the text alone, confirmed both theorems by exhaustive enumeration for every odd q from 3 to 17, and recommended acceptance with minor revisions, which were made (an explicit arc argument, the q = 5 counts, the q = 3 case via the Petersen graph, clearer wording).

Computer-assisted. The upper bound rests on finite computations with 27 x 27 Boolean matrices (T^2 = T^4, the far-pairs lemma, and an exhaustive search over the 2^36 edge sets of three consecutive units with monotone pruning); the transfer model is checked against direct colouring of the explicit graph for every set of at most two edges when q = 3, 5, 7.
The question for other snarks is open: the Petersen graph also gives 9 (its 10 claw sets), J_3 gives 15.

Knuth's exercise and answer are paraphrased from Pre-Fascicle 7A (5 December 2024), the frozen draft of Volume 4 Fascicle 7, fetched from the Internet Archive; they are cited, not reproduced. Whether the result is new was checked only against that answer and a short literature search.
